subject: Behavioral Economics
title: Strategic Voting
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Strategic Voting.

hook.text: You prefer candidate A but vote for B because only B can beat C, whom you dislike most.

buildup.text: Strategic Voting sets up the incentives, biases, and tradeoffs driving the choice.

discovery.text: Gibbard and Satterthwaite proved no voting system is immune to strategic manipulation.

twist.text: Polls enable strategic voting by revealing who can win. Without polls, voters express true preferences more often.

climax.text: Voting systems shape strategy. Ranked-choice reduces strategic voting by letting you express a true first choice safely.

punchline.text: Every voting system can be gamed. The best ones make gaming unnecessary.

quiz.question: What did the Gibbard-Satterthwaite theorem prove?
options: Some voting systems are perfectly fair
No voting system is completely immune to strategic manipulation
Strategic voting always produces the best outcomes
